m.chalisa.cau1: First I bow my head to the Guru, and fix my mind on the feet of Śrī Hari.
m.chalisa.cau2: Friend, I sing a wondrous song; by holding to it one's boat is carried across.
m.chalisa.cau3: Arjuna said: Listen, Lord: you have told of your many forms.
m.chalisa.cau4: I have not understood the difference between them at all; be gracious, wise one, and tell me again.
m.chalisa.cau5: One meditates on you every day and sets his mind on you with devotion,
m.chalisa.cau6: sings your virtues night and day, and nothing other than you pleases his mind;
m.chalisa.cau7: he repeats your name day and night and speaks of nothing else.
m.chalisa.cau8: The other meditates on the formless, and calls it imperishable, unseen and beginningless.
m.chalisa.cau9: Both are given to meditation; which of them is the better, son of Nanda?
m.chalisa.cau10: The Lord said to Arjuna: Listen, dear one, and give it some attention.
m.chalisa.cau11: One who repeats my name and has others repeat it, whose eyes fill with tears of love,
m.chalisa.cau12: who wants nothing but me, and sings my virtues night and day,
m.chalisa.cau13: whose hair stands on end again and again when he hears my name spoken,
m.chalisa.cau14: those whose thread does not break for a moment — their faith is firm and boundless.
m.chalisa.cau15: One who is joined to me and fixes his mind in meditation, and in meditation is overwhelmed,
m.chalisa.cau16: whose throat is choked so that he cannot speak, whose mind and intellect are absorbed in me,
m.chalisa.cau17: who forgets shame, fear and pride, and has no awareness left of his own body:
m.chalisa.cau18: one who fixes his mind in meditation in this way is called the best of yogīs.
m.chalisa.cau19: Whoever meditates on the form without attributes, the complete Brahman, unmoving and incomparable,
m.chalisa.cau20: which all the Vedas call formless, and whose depth the mind and intellect cannot find,
m.chalisa.cau21: which never perishes, which pervades all things like the sky,
m.chalisa.cau22: which is steadfast, beginningless and bliss itself, which only a rare yogī knows;
m.chalisa.cau23: who meditates so without a break, and regards all as one and the same,
m.chalisa.cau24: keeps his mind and senses under his control, and never tastes the pleasures of the senses,
m.chalisa.cau25: and is devoted to the welfare of all beings: such is their true creed.
m.chalisa.cau26: They too reach me alone, and surely go to the supreme goal.
m.chalisa.cau27: The fruit of both is the same, but meditation on the attributeless is hard.
m.chalisa.cau28: As long as there is pride in the mind, it is hard to gain knowledge.
m.chalisa.cau29: For those whose love is for the attributeless, the practice and its rules are hard to accomplish.
m.chalisa.cau30: The mind has no support on which to rest; so that practice is hard beyond measure.
m.chalisa.cau31: The easy way, that of Brahman with attributes, I have told you.
m.chalisa.cau32: Offering to me all his countless works, sacrifice, charity and the rest,
m.chalisa.cau33: one who fixes his mind on me unwavering, regards me as his very life,
m.chalisa.cau34: breaks off his love for all the world, and regards me as his friend,
m.chalisa.cau35: who is absorbed in love beyond all measure and sees this world as empty:
m.chalisa.cau36: those whose mind is always in me, friend, I love them dearly.
m.chalisa.cau37: Becoming the boatman, I row the boat and bring them across the ocean of worldly existence.
m.chalisa.cau38: This is the highest knowledge of all; so meditate on me.
m.chalisa.cau39: Then you will become like me; know that what I say is true.
m.chalisa.cau40: Whoever walks according to this, he too crosses the ocean of worldly existence.
